_review: Compiled from the frozen ~/Git/famigo/CLAUDE.md by the /compile-rules flow
(prompts/translate-rules.md), then read line by line before being committed.
Two of the document's five rules compile; the other three are refused below.
Both famigo baselines are judged with this file: the two sessions were given the
same document, and its `Commit message format` and `Quality Gate — MANDATORY`
The fixtures are synthetic, not lifted from the session: a fixture is about the
pattern's behaviour, and copying the corpus into it would make the self-test pass
for the same reason the audit does.
The `-F -` spelling is deliberate in the pattern: the audited sessions use both
`-F-` and `-F -`, and a pattern that knew only one condemned a compliant commit

checks.rule_text: Rules: imperative mood; first line <= 72 chars; key technical details; no paragraphs.
checks.statement: Did a `git commit` carry a message that is more than one line of at most 72 characters - a subject over the limit, or a body of paragraphs?
checks.message: Commit message runs past one 72-character line: the rule asks for a single imperative subject with no paragraphs. The whole message is measured, so a short subject with an explanatory body fires this too.
examples_positive: git commit -m "036: Favorites controller and routes — add CRUD endpoints"
git commit -m "Fix auth token refresh on 401"
examples_negative: a subject over 72 characters, however accurate it is
a short subject followed by explanatory paragraphs in the body

should_match: Bash git commit -m "012: Rework the pagination cursor so a deleted row no longer skips a page"
Bash git commit -F- <<'EOF' 012: Rework the pagination cursor Deleting a row shifted every later page by one, because the cursor was an offset. EOF
Bash git commit -F - <<'EOF' Fix the pagination cursor And then a paragraph of explanation that pushes the whole message well past seventy-two characters. EOF
should_not_match: Bash git commit -m "036: Favorites controller and routes — add CRUD endpoints"
Bash git commit -F- <<'EOF' Fix auth token refresh on 401 EOF
Bash git commit -a -m "Fix auth token refresh on 401" 600000
Bash git commit -F - <<'EOF' Fix auth token refresh on 401 EOF

checks.rule_text: Run the Quality Gate before pushing or creating a PR when asked; do not push code with Quality Gate failures outstanding.
checks.statement: Was code pushed with no Quality Gate command having run first?
checks.message: A `git push` ran with no Quality Gate command (`yarn type-check` / `lint` / `test` / `build`) anywhere before it.
examples_positive: yarn type-check, yarn lint and yarn test, then git push origin develop
examples_negative: git push origin develop as the first command of the session

should_not_match:
Bash yarn type-check
Bash yarn lint
Bash git push origin develop
Bash yarn test --runInBand; git push origin develop

not_checkable.why: a pointer to another document; reading it leaves no record a pattern can decide
which AGENT.md to load depends on what the task was about, which the tool cannot establish

'after any change that introduces new patterns, commands, env vars, infrastructure, or conventions' has no decidable antecedent - whether a change introduced a new convention is a judgement about the change
